knowledgeUnits.heading: Understand the existing program before editing

leadVisual.title: Understand the existing program before editing

coreExplanation: The program receives three validated INTEGER quantities and outputs one sum. It does not validate raw input, process a sentinel or subtract bookings from Available. Preserve those assumptions while analysing this amendment.
Total is initialised once, updated for every input and displayed once after the loop. Trace those statements before proposing new code.

The additional count needs an INTEGER declaration, zero initialisation, a qualifying condition, an increment and a final output. The original total, input count and update remain. A heading saying “add group count” is not enough to locate all affected operations.

learningCycle.observe: Use 2, 3, 6. The total is 11, while two bookings meet the new group threshold. Counting qualifying bookings is different from totalling their seats.

stimulus.title: The existing booking report
items: Read exactly three already valid requests, each an integer from 1 to 6.
Output the sum of their Seats values. Requests are independent; the sum is not a remaining-capacity calculation.
The new request is to report how many bookings contain at least 3 seats as well, without changing the original total.

learningCycle.question: Which old behaviour must remain, and which new information is missing?

prerequisite.title: Recall count versus total
prerequisite.body: A count increases by 1 for each qualifying item. A total increases by the item’s numeric value. Both need initialisation before repetition and final output after the relevant inputs have been processed.

steps.title: State the current contract
steps.body: The program receives three validated INTEGER quantities and outputs one sum. It does not validate raw input, process a sentinel or subtract bookings from Available. Preserve those assumptions while analysing this amendment.

steps.title: Read the actual placement of operations
steps.body: Total is initialised once, updated for every input and displayed once after the loop. Trace those statements before proposing new code.
steps.code:
DECLARE Index, Seats, Total : INTEGER
Total <- 0
FOR Index <- 1 TO 3
    INPUT Seats
    Total <- Total + Seats
NEXT Index
OUTPUT Total

steps.title: Make an impact list for the new requirement
steps.body: The additional count needs an INTEGER declaration, zero initialisation, a qualifying condition, an increment and a final output. The original total, input count and update remain. A heading saying “add group count” is not enough to locate all affected operations.

worked.title: Establish a baseline for the amendment
worked.setup: Run a manual trace using input 2, 3, 6.

steps.title: Trace the original values
steps.body: Total progresses 0 → 2 → 5 → 11. There is one final output, 11. No group counter currently exists.

steps.title: Write the new expected outcome before editing
steps.body: The enhanced program should still output 11, then output 2 for the number of requests with at least 3 seats. The requested new output does not replace the old one.

worked.conclusion: A baseline identifies the old contract, current implementation and behaviour that the change must preserve.

check.prompt: Why would replacing Total <- Total + Seats with Total <- Total + 1 fail the change request?
check.answer: It would change the original sum into a count and lose the required total. Add a separate counter and retain the existing total update.

learningCycle.takeaway: Trace the old program and define the preservation requirements before designing the amendment.
learningCycle.bridge: Next place every part of the additional count and choose tests that would expose incorrect placement.

knowledgeUnits.heading: Add the new result and test old and new behaviour

leadVisual.title: Add the new result and test old and new behaviour

coreExplanation: Declare GroupBookings as INTEGER and set it to 0 before the loop. Starting it inside the loop would erase earlier qualifying bookings.
Retain Total <- Total + Seats for every input. Then use IF Seats >= 3 to increment GroupBookings by 1. The group test does not belong in an ELSE that would prevent its seats entering Total.
Place both output statements after NEXT so they describe the complete set. Keep the original result first, followed by the added count.

Use 2 and 3 around the new inclusive threshold. Include no qualifying bookings, all qualifying bookings and several early qualifying bookings. For every set, check that the total matches the old program as well as checking the new count.

learningCycle.observe: Imagine initialising GroupBookings inside the loop. Then imagine displaying it before the loop finishes. Explain which required output each placement would break.
learningCycle.question: Where must the new counter start, change and be displayed?

prerequisite.title: Recall overlapping responsibilities
prerequisite.body: Every request contributes its seats to Total. Some also add one to GroupBookings. These are not mutually exclusive alternatives: a qualifying request must contribute to both results.

steps.title: Declare and initialise once
steps.body: Declare GroupBookings as INTEGER and set it to 0 before the loop. Starting it inside the loop would erase earlier qualifying bookings.

steps.title: Update at the correct scope
steps.body: Retain Total <- Total + Seats for every input. Then use IF Seats >= 3 to increment GroupBookings by 1. The group test does not belong in an ELSE that would prevent its seats entering Total.

steps.title: Output both final results
steps.body: Place both output statements after NEXT so they describe the complete set. Keep the original result first, followed by the added count.
steps.code:
DECLARE Index, Seats, Total : INTEGER
DECLARE GroupBookings : INTEGER
Total <- 0
GroupBookings <- 0
FOR Index <- 1 TO 3
    INPUT Seats
    Total <- Total + Seats
    IF Seats >= 3 THEN
        GroupBookings <- GroupBookings + 1
    ENDIF
NEXT Index
OUTPUT Total
OUTPUT GroupBookings

steps.title: Test boundaries, accumulation and preservation
steps.body: Use 2 and 3 around the new inclusive threshold. Include no qualifying bookings, all qualifying bookings and several early qualifying bookings. For every set, check that the total matches the old program as well as checking the new count.

worked.title: Expose a misplaced reset
worked.setup: Compare the correct enhancement with a version that resets GroupBookings to 0 on every loop visit.

steps.title: Use a sequence with repeated qualifying items
steps.body: For 3, 4, 6 the correct outputs are total 13 and group count 3. The reset-inside-loop version ends with group count 1, so this sequence distinguishes the fault.

steps.title: Transfer to overlapping grade categories
steps.body: In the separate mark example, Mark >= 70 is a merit and also a pass at >= 50. Two independent IF statements update both counts; ELSE would incorrectly exclude one. Input 49, 50, 69, 70 must yield 3 passes and 1 merit.
steps.code:
DECLARE Index : INTEGER
DECLARE Mark : INTEGER
DECLARE PassCount : INTEGER
DECLARE MeritCount : INTEGER
PassCount <- 0
MeritCount <- 0
FOR Index <- 1 TO 4
    INPUT Mark
    IF Mark >= 50 THEN
        PassCount <- PassCount + 1
    ENDIF
    IF Mark >= 70 THEN
        MeritCount <- MeritCount + 1
    ENDIF
NEXT Index
OUTPUT PassCount
OUTPUT MeritCount

worked.conclusion: Use complete datasets that would fail under plausible wrong amendments, not just one convenient example.

check.prompt: For bookings 3, 1, 1, what are Total and GroupBookings? Why is this also useful for testing a counter reset inside the loop?
check.answer: Total is 5 and GroupBookings is 1. A faulty counter reset on each iteration would lose the first qualifying booking and finish at 0 because the last two requests do not qualify.

learningCycle.takeaway: A complete amendment aligns declaration, initialisation, processing and output, then verifies changed and preserved behaviour.
learningCycle.bridge: An interface change reaches beyond one function body: callers and test inputs must change with it.

knowledgeUnits.heading: Change the interface and every affected caller

leadVisual.title: Change the interface and every affected caller

coreExplanation: The function now needs two inputs. Replace the fixed upper bound with the supplied Limit, but preserve the lower bound and BOOLEAN return. Document that Limit itself has already been validated.
Declare Limit and read it before Seats. Pass Seats first and Limit second at every call. An old one-argument call no longer matches the header; reversed arguments compare the wrong roles.
This small program checks one integer request against one selected limit. It does not read a different limit for each part of a calculation.

With Limit 6, old accepted and rejected quantities must behave as before. With Limit 8, Seats 7 now passes, while 9 fails. Include Seats 0 to protect the unchanged minimum. Each fixture must supply the limit before the quantity.

learningCycle.observe: Locate the source of Limit, its position in the call and the comparison that uses it. Two INTEGER arguments can have the correct types yet be passed in the wrong order.

stimulus.title: A configurable booking rule
items: The old function IsValid(Seats) checks the fixed range 1–6.
The new version reads one Limit before one Seats value. Limit is already validated as an integer from 1 to 12.
Change the function to IsValid(Seats, Limit). Keep its BOOLEAN result and accept Seats from 1 through Limit inclusive.

learningCycle.question: Why is adding a parameter to the function header only part of the change?

prerequisite.title: Recall an ordered interface
prerequisite.body: Formal parameters appear in the function header; arguments appear in its call. Number, order, types and intended roles must agree. A returned BOOLEAN is used by the caller’s selection.

links.label: Review ordered function interfaces and returns

steps.title: Revise the contract before its implementation
steps.body: The function now needs two inputs. Replace the fixed upper bound with the supplied Limit, but preserve the lower bound and BOOLEAN return. Document that Limit itself has already been validated.

steps.title: Update the caller’s state and input sequence
steps.body: Declare Limit and read it before Seats. Pass Seats first and Limit second at every call. An old one-argument call no longer matches the header; reversed arguments compare the wrong roles.

steps.title: Show the complete revised connection
steps.body: This small program checks one integer request against one selected limit. It does not read a different limit for each part of a calculation.
steps.code:
FUNCTION IsValid(BYVAL Seats : INTEGER, BYVAL Limit : INTEGER) RETURNS BOOLEAN
    RETURN (Seats >= 1) AND (Seats <= Limit)
ENDFUNCTION

DECLARE Limit, Seats : INTEGER
INPUT Limit
INPUT Seats
IF IsValid(Seats, Limit) THEN
    OUTPUT "Accepted"
ELSE
    OUTPUT "Rejected"
ENDIF

steps.title: Update tests and examples to the new interface
steps.body: With Limit 6, old accepted and rejected quantities must behave as before. With Limit 8, Seats 7 now passes, while 9 fails. Include Seats 0 to protect the unchanged minimum. Each fixture must supply the limit before the quantity.

worked.title: Distinguish compatibility from new behaviour
worked.setup: Test the revised function and its complete caller.

steps.title: Check the old parameter setting
steps.body: Inputs 6, 6 must display Accepted and 6, 7 must display Rejected. These reproduce the old upper-limit rule.

steps.title: Check a deliberately different setting
steps.body: Inputs 8, 7 must display Accepted. If the function body still compares with 6, it incorrectly rejects the request. Inputs 8, 9 must display Rejected. A reversed call IsValid(Limit, Seats) would make the latter comparison 8 <= 9 and wrongly accept it.

worked.conclusion: Header, body, callers, input fixtures and documentation are one connected change.

check.prompt: The header becomes IsValid(Seats, Limit), but the function still returns Seats <= 6. Why can tests using only Limit 6 miss the fault?
check.answer: Those tests reproduce the old fixed rule, so the hard-coded 6 appears correct. Use a different valid limit, such as Limit 8 with Seats 7, to prove the new parameter actually changes the decision. Retain the lower-bound check too.

learningCycle.takeaway: Interface amendments require coordinated changes at every definition, call and dependent test.
learningCycle.bridge: Stored record formats are also interfaces. Changing what data may contain can require a different way to find field boundaries.

knowledgeUnits.heading: Preserve field boundaries when data changes

leadVisual.title: Preserve field boundaries when data changes

coreExplanation: Delimiter-separated fields work only when the delimiter is excluded or handled by a defined escaping rule. The new fields can contain it, so the old “split everywhere” reader is no longer valid. Both writer and reader depend on the format.

For each added field, store its length as exactly two decimal digits followed immediately by that many characters. The limit 99 makes two digits sufficient. A one-character field begins 01, an empty field 00. Unseparated variable-width lengths would introduce another ambiguous boundary.

Preserve the three original fields and their agreed delimiters, including a delimiter after the email before the added section. Read two digits as a length, then exactly that many characters. Repeat for the next field. Characters inside those spans are data, even when they look like delimiters.

Update writing, reading, format documentation and fixtures together. Check an empty added field, one containing the old delimiter and a maximum-length field. If line breaks are possible, first encode them into a single-line representation and define lengths consistently for that stored representation.

learningCycle.observe: Try storing the added value A|B. A reader that splits at every | would treat one value as two fields. The format must describe boundaries without mistaking field data for separators.

stimulus.title: A changed record requirement
items: A booking record stores BookingID, Name and Email, separated by |. These original fields are guaranteed not to contain |.
Two new encoded fields may contain any visible character, including |. Each has length 0–99.
The whole record must remain on one physical line. How will a reader know where each added field ends?

learningCycle.question: Can choosing a different separator solve a field that may contain any separator?

prerequisite.title: Recall text records and string length
prerequisite.body: A text record needs a defined way to separate its fields. LENGTH counts characters; a substring operation extracts a specified number of characters. Leading zeros in a fixed-width length are meaningful text. Read each paper’s supplied string interface before using its function names.

links.label: Review text records and file operations

steps.title: Analyse the old assumption that no longer holds
steps.body: Delimiter-separated fields work only when the delimiter is excluded or handled by a defined escaping rule. The new fields can contain it, so the old “split everywhere” reader is no longer valid. Both writer and reader depend on the format.

steps.title: Choose an unambiguous length representation
steps.body: For each added field, store its length as exactly two decimal digits followed immediately by that many characters. The limit 99 makes two digits sufficient. A one-character field begins 01, an empty field 00. Unseparated variable-width lengths would introduce another ambiguous boundary.

steps.title: Find the new section and read by length
steps.body: Preserve the three original fields and their agreed delimiters, including a delimiter after the email before the added section. Read two digits as a length, then exactly that many characters. Repeat for the next field. Characters inside those spans are data, even when they look like delimiters.

steps.title: Amend both sides and verify the new contract
steps.body: Update writing, reading, format documentation and fixtures together. Check an empty added field, one containing the old delimiter and a maximum-length field. If line breaks are possible, first encode them into a single-line representation and define lengths consistently for that stored representation.

worked.title: Decode a record with an embedded separator
worked.setup: The teacher-written record is B004|Mina|mina@example.org|03A|B02xy. The new values are A|B and xy.

steps.title: Locate the section boundary
steps.body: The first three delimiters bound the original BookingID, Name and Email fields. After the email delimiter, the reader changes to the new length-prefixed format.

steps.title: Read the two new fields
steps.body: Read 03, then exactly A, | and B. That internal | belongs to the first field. Read 02 next, then x and y. The consumed characters now end at the record end. Both values are recovered without choosing a forbidden separator.

steps.title: Connect the format change to program enhancement
steps.body: The implementation must write and read matching formats. An amended writer paired with the old split-at-every-separator reader still fails. Use the same analysis–impact–amend–verify method as for the changed function interface.

worked.conclusion: A reliable enhancement revises the assumptions and every component that depends on them.

check.prompt: How would you store the added fields "" and "A|B" using two-digit lengths? Why does picking # as a new separator not solve the general problem?
check.answer: The added section is 0003A|B: 00 introduces an empty first field; 03 introduces the three-character second field. Choosing # is insufficient because the new data may also contain #.

learningCycle.takeaway: When a data assumption changes, revise the format and all readers and writers that depend on it.
learningCycle.bridge: The complete development method is now connected: agree a requirement, design, implement, test and maintain its dependent parts.

steps.title: Connect the format change to program enhancement
steps.body: The implementation must write and read matching formats. An amended writer paired with the old split-at-every-separator reader still fails. Use the same analysis–impact–amend–verify method as for the changed function interface.

workedExample.conclusion: A reliable enhancement revises the assumptions and every component that depends on them.

knowledgeUnits.heading: Section 9: Algorithm design and problem-solving

leadVisual.title: S9 review route

coreExplanation: Begin with the required result and retain the facts that determine it. Decompose the task into cooperating responsibilities, choose meaningful identifiers and refine the processing until the rules and execution order are explicit. The resulting IPO, pseudocode and flowchart should describe the same solution.

Challenge a completed algorithm at decision boundaries and loop limits. Follow each path using actual values, checking initialisation, new inputs, updates and the final output. A convincing design combines correct logic with a representation that another programmer can implement without guessing.

workedExample.title: Count accepted parcels

knowledgeUnits.heading: Section 10: Data types and structures

leadVisual.title: S10 review route

coreExplanation: Choose each value's type before grouping values: record fields may have different types, whereas an array has a declared element type and explicit bounds. One index selects a 1D element; two select a 2D element. Write complete declarations, field access and bounded iteration before tracing the resulting values.

For array processing, linear search checks consecutive elements and reports a matching position or absence; bubble sort uses complete adjacent swaps. Files retain results between runs through the appropriate read, write or append mode. ADTs specify data and operations: use LIFO for a stack, FIFO for a queue and links for a linked list, and keep the array implementation's active state consistent after each operation.

workedExample.title: Trace data through a small booking system

knowledgeUnits.heading: Section 11: Programming

leadVisual.title: Programming review checks

coreExplanation: Translate the stated rules into declarations, expressions and correctly placed control structures. Read supplied routine interfaces before calling them. A complete solution defines values before use, respects condition boundaries and makes progress toward the stopping condition.

Connect subprograms through arguments, returned values and intentional reference updates. In this review, a parking session costs 3 per whole hour; positive integer hours are entered until sentinel zero. A charge function returns each fee and an accumulation procedure updates the running total. The first input may already be zero.

workedExample.title: Combine a charge function and accumulation procedure

knowledgeUnits.heading: Section 12: Software development

leadVisual.title: S12 review route

coreExplanation: Connect each development decision to observable evidence: requirements and project constraints guide the life cycle; a hierarchy and labelled interfaces guide implementation; states and transitions document event-dependent behaviour. Use a trace to check that the resulting algorithm implements the intended rules.

Choose tests for the risks being examined and record their expected results before running them. After delivery, identify why a change is needed, analyse its impact, make the requested amendment and check both changed and preserved behaviour. A category name alone cannot demonstrate any of these practical skills.
